purpose: Bounded methodological follow-up to the closed comparative pilot, requested by the user; development only
question: Does a component incompatible with motion reversal account for a practically relevant part of the frozen predictors' error?
models: Three measured 3000-step checkpoints, all nine spatial-null 3000-step checkpoints, three GRU 500-step checkpoints
transformation: Reverse the complete eight-frame sequence and negate its two-dimensional velocity. Retain original train-only normalization.
diagnostic: p=f(x), q=f(reverse(x)), odd=(p-q)/2, even=(p+q)/2. Evaluate p against y, q against -y, odd against y, and squared norm of even.
identity: Mean paired forward/reversed MSE minus odd MSE equals mean squared norm of even. This identity is not an empirical improvement claim or a biological mechanism.
candidate_gate: Consider a single-factor training reversal-augmentation experiment only if odd validation EPE improves at least 5 percent for each of three measured seeds AND each of three spatial-null row means, with mean counterfactual EPE not worsened in either family. Gate is a practical development decision, not statistical significance.
if_gate_fails: Do not schedule reversal-augmentation training from this diagnostic alone; preserve negative evidence and retain the no-scaling decision.
if_gate_passes: Specify bounded matched training with reversal augmentation, preserving one causal forward pass at inference. Do not treat the two-pass diagnostic as a deployed improvement or launch GPU automatically.
limits: Same reused development clips; reversed clips are dependent on their originals. No new confirmation, no test selection, no clips excluded, no anatomical attribution, no extra training. Two-pass retrospective symmetrization cannot replace the causal online model and doubles forward work.
